result.title: Protocol-Aware Auditing of Domain-Blind Feature Attribution in Network Intrusion Detection
result.comment: Accepted as a poster at the LXAI Research Workshop, NeurIPS 2026; 6 figures
result.summary: Feature-attribution methods can query rule-violating network states through perturbations, coalitions, references, paths, and ablations, making explanations and their evaluation sensitive to model behavior outside the operational domain. We formalize this failure mode as domain blindness and prove valid-query invariance: when models agree on the required oracle information within a declared rule-valid set, a procedure confined to that set returns the same attribution. We instantiate one protocol-aware query-control principle in LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and DeepLIFT and audit paired configurations across four NIDS datasets and three classifier families. In six settings where standard LIME reports perfect top-feature repeatability, PA-LIME reveals substantial variability, with a mean of 0.575. Under FGSM followed by protocol repair, PA-DeepLIFT and PA-IG achieve the largest attribution-similarity curve areas, 0.452 and 0.413, while mean within-PA rank agreement rises to 0.366 from 0.217. PA-XAI therefore turns structured domain assumptions into explicit, testable controls for explanation auditing; support modeling, raw-flow reconstruction, and adaptive explanation attacks provide complementary validation layers.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把特征归因方法在规则无效域中查询所导致的脆弱性形式化为「domain blindness」，并给出有效查询不变性结论，在 LIME、SHAP、IG、DeepLIFT 中加入协议约束式查询控制，于四个 NIDS 数据集上审计归因稳定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅在被声明为合法的输入集合内做扰动」这一约束思想，可能为 VLM 中以遮挡或扰动评估视觉证据贡献时产生的越界输入问题提供可核查的评价视角。
